items.criterion: The worked canonical string derives the identifier the brief pins.
items.judgment: Yes when the derivation reproduces the pinned identifier byte for byte.
items.evidence: the identifier returned for the worked example settings

items.criterion: A saved preset carries the identifier its own settings derive to.
items.judgment: Yes when the returned identifier equals the independently recomputed one.
items.evidence: the save response compared against the recomputed derivation

items.criterion: Two concurrent saves of identical settings leave one preset row.
items.judgment: Yes when exactly one row carries the derived identifier afterwards.
items.evidence: the preset row count for the derived identifier

items.criterion: A private preset refuses its own address to every caller but its owner.
items.judgment: Yes when all three non-owning callers receive the not-found refusal.
items.evidence: the status returned to a signed-out caller, a reader and a second author

items.criterion: A private preset's refusal matches the refusal for an identifier never created.
items.judgment: Yes when both the status and the body match.
items.evidence: the two refusals compared

items.criterion: A private preset's rendered export is refused with the preset.
items.judgment: Yes when all three non-owning callers receive the not-found refusal.
items.evidence: the status returned by the export route to each non-owning caller

items.criterion: A rendered export exists in the bucket at the key its render row names.
items.judgment: Yes when the object store reports the key present.
items.evidence: an out-of-band read of the declared bucket

items.criterion: A stored object's key carries the digest of the bytes served for it.
items.judgment: Yes when the digest of the served bytes appears in the stored key.
items.evidence: the served export rehashed against the stored key

items.criterion: Two renders producing identical bytes occupy one stored object.
items.judgment: Yes when the bucket gains no object on the second identical render.
items.evidence: the bucket listing before the second render compared with after

items.criterion: A refused render leaves the bucket unchanged.
items.judgment: Yes when the bucket listing is identical before the refusal to after.
items.evidence: the bucket listing around an oversized render

items.criterion: Publishing one preset twice leaves one gallery entry.
items.judgment: Yes when the entry count for that preset is one.
items.evidence: the gallery entry count for the published preset

items.criterion: A fork records exactly one parent.
items.judgment: Yes when the child row names the original as its parent.
items.evidence: the stored parent reference on the forked preset

items.criterion: A fork raises the parent's stored fork count by one.
items.judgment: Yes when the stored count rises by exactly one.
items.evidence: the parent's stored fork count before the fork compared with after

items.criterion: A deleted preset carrying forks is tombstoned rather than removed.
items.judgment: Yes when the row survives with its state set to tombstoned.
items.evidence: the stored row after the delete

items.criterion: A child resolves its ancestry through a tombstoned parent.
items.judgment: Yes when the child keeps its parent reference after the parent is tombstoned.
items.evidence: the child row and its detail route after the parent is deleted

items.criterion: A reader session is refused at every author-only endpoint.
items.judgment: Yes when all four attempted writes are refused by the server.
items.evidence: the statuses returned to a reader session on save, render, publish and fork

items.criterion: A denied reader write leaves every table unchanged.
items.judgment: Yes when the preset, entry and render counts are unchanged.
items.evidence: the three row counts before the denied write compared with after

items.criterion: An author is refused on another account's preset.
items.judgment: Yes when edit, publish, delete and render are all refused.
items.evidence: the statuses returned to a second author on the four write routes

items.criterion: A forbidden cross-author write leaves the row unchanged.
items.judgment: Yes when the title and the state are the same afterwards.
items.evidence: the stored row before the forbidden write compared with after

items.criterion: The tile grid is served in the stored position order.
items.judgment: Yes when the served order matches the stored order.
items.evidence: the served tile list compared with the seeded rows

items.criterion: A retired generator keeps its route while leaving the tile grid.
items.judgment: Yes when the route resolves and the grid omits it.
items.evidence: the generator detail route and the served tile list

items.criterion: An unlisted preset resolves by address while staying out of the gallery.
items.judgment: Yes when the address resolves and the gallery omits it.
items.evidence: the preset detail route and the gallery listing

items.criterion: Every internal link on every public route resolves.
items.judgment: Yes when no internal link answers with a client or server error.
items.evidence: every internal link found on the public routes, followed

items.criterion: Invalid form input is rejected before anything is written.
items.judgment: Yes when the row count is unchanged after the rejection.
items.evidence: the report row count around an invalid submission
